213000.name: Durgan's Gate

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Durgar's Gate - The Doors To The Dwarven Kingdom.

213000.description:
Durgan's Gate is a great arch hewn from the mountain, its tall doors of
iron and stone swung wide and left to rust open on their hinges. Rows of
bearded kings are carved up the jambs, their stone beards chipped by
thieves. To the south the doors open on the barren badlands outside, and
a bar thick as a man's waist lies split on the flagstones. North the
Main Tunnel leads into the dim city.

213001.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies Durgan's Gate.

213001.description:
The air here is fresher and colder, carrying a faint taste of open
mountain from the south. A pair of empty lantern-hooks beside a deep-set
doorframe mark where the gate-wardens once checked travellers' papers.
The paving is cracked and heaved by the cold that creeps in from
outside. North the road runs on into the tunnel, and south lies Durgan's
Gate.

213002.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

213002.description:
Painted warnings in an angular dwarven script have been daubed on the
wall at shoulder height, now flaking to red dust. Beneath them stands an
old toll-post, a stout iron-bound beam with a slot for coins that has
long been empty. The road is rutted from the wagons of merchants who
once paid to pass. North it climbs gently toward the heart of the
tunnel, while south it runs to Durgan's Gate.

213003.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

213003.description:
This reach of the Main Tunnel is roughly cut and uneven, as if the
workers laid down their picks before the final dressing. Long chisel-
marks run slantwise across the rock, and chips of broken stone lie
scattered in the gutters. A rotted rope still hangs from two hooks
across the way, set there to mark the end of some old repair. The tunnel
runs on north to a bend and south toward the gate.

213004.name: A Bend In The Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

213004.description:
The passage bends here, coming up from the south and turning to run east
toward the halls. The corner is squared off by a block of black marble
set into the floor, carved with the wind-rose of the dwarven road
wardens. A crack runs across it from edge to edge. The roof is lower
than elsewhere and sweats with a cold condensation that drips steadily
onto the stone.

213005.name: The Main Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies The Ambassadors Halls.

west.description: To the west lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

213005.description:
A narrow stretch of tunnel runs between the Ambassadors Halls to the
east and a bend to the west. Little care went into its cutting, for it
was only a servants' way, and the ceiling is low enough that a tall man
must stoop. Bare hooks line the rock, where cloaks and lanterns once
hung for the footmen of departed embassies. A bitter smell of cold ash
lingers in the air.

213006.name: The Ambassadors Halls

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies The Main Tunnel.

213006.description:
The Ambassadors Halls open as a line of high, echoing chambers, where
the envoys of far kingdoms were once lodged in splendour. Each doorway
is flanked by a carved pillar bearing the crest of some distant house,
and the doors themselves are chained shut, their lacquer peeling in long
curls. Mosaic floors of coloured stone have lost half their tesserae to
thieves. A passage runs north into the Main Tunnel, and another leads
west along the dim flank of the halls.

213007.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Ambassadors Halls.

213007.description:
The tunnel brightens and broadens, for ahead lie the Ambassadors Halls,
and the masons here took more care. Slender fluted pilasters stand at
regular intervals along both walls, each capped with a leaf-shaped
capital gone black with smoke. A strip of faded carpet runs down the
middle of the road, worn through to the threads. The way runs north back
to a bend and south into the halls.

213008.name: A Bend In The Tunnel

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies The Main Tunnel.

213008.description:
The road turns a sharp corner here, coming in from the west and plunging
away south through a tall, narrow passage. A heavy iron ring is sunk in
the rock at the turning, and a coil of chain is still fastened to it,
rusted into a single mass. The walls bear the dark prints of countless
hands that steadied themselves at the corner. The air from the south is
warmer and carries faint scents of incense and polished wood.

213009.name: The Main Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies The Main Tunnel.

213009.description:
A long frieze of marching dwarves is carved along the wall at head
height, axes shouldered and beards braided, though the chisel-work ends
in a ragged line where the commission ran out. Below it the plaster has
fallen away in broad leprous patches. The road continues east to a bend
and west toward a lower stretch. Somewhere far off, a slow drip counts
out the hours.

213010.name: The Main Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies The Main Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

213010.description:
The road runs straight east and west here through a low, wide passage,
its roof held up by squat columns left standing as the dwarves cut the
rock away. Between the columns stretch shallow alcoves, once resting
places for drovers, now bare floors littered with ash. A faint draught
blows through from the east, bringing the smell of old dust and distant
smoke. Behind you to the west the road dips toward a bend.

213011.name: A Bend In The Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

east.description: To the east lies The Main Tunnel.

213011.description:
The tunnel bends here from its northward course to run east, and the
outer face of the curve is polished smooth where wagons scraped it going
round. A lamp-niche in the rock is choked with glass and soot. Beyond
the corner the passage narrows and the roof sinks lower, pressing down
with the weight of the mountain. The air smells of cold iron and damp
wool.

213012.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

213012.description:
A cross-vault of rough stone arches over the road here, and a pair of
square pillars stand at the middle of the way, leaving a narrow lane to
either side. Initials and tally-marks have been scratched into them by
generations of passing drovers. The floor is dusted with fine pale grit
that muffles every step. North the passage runs back toward the gate,
and south it comes to a bend.

213013.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

213013.description:
Water seeps from a hairline crack in the vault and runs down the rock in
a bright thread to a drainage channel cut along the road's edge. The
stone beneath it is stained green and slick, and a cold dampness hangs
in the air. Pale crusts of mineral have grown over a row of carved
dwarf-runes, hiding what they once said. The tunnel runs on north toward
the gate and south into the dark.

213014.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Gate To The Stronghold.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

213014.description:
Beyond the gate chamber the tunnel falls quiet, and the noise behind you
fades to a faint metallic ticking as the old iron cools and settles. The
rock here is blank and unadorned, plainly cut by builders who cared for
strength over beauty. Scraps of rotted sacking and a broken wheel lie
piled in a niche. The tunnel runs on south, and the dark seems to lean
in from that way.

213015.name: The Gate To The Stronghold

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies The Hall Of Splendor.

213015.description:
The road swells into a vast vaulted chamber where the great gate to the
stronghold stands, a towering arch of black iron and bronze whose
portcullis hangs half-raised, jammed by rust. Barricades of timber and
overturned carts crowd the flagstones beneath it, and tattered battle-
banners droop from the twin towers. A bronze-studded door in the west
wall leads into the Hall of Splendor. The Main Tunnel runs away north
and south from the chamber.

extra_descs.portcullis gate banners:
The portcullis bars are as thick as a dwarf's thigh and crusted with
rust, but scraped bright where something heavy has been dragged beneath
them. Beyond the half-raised teeth, a ramp of dressed stone climbs into
the stronghold.

213016.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Gate To The Stronghold.

213016.description:
The tunnel widens and its walls begin to show their old splendour, with
panels of pale stone inlaid in the rock and cut with chains of
interlocking runes. Most of the inlay has been prised out, leaving raw
sockets. The road runs south to the Gate To The Stronghold, and the air
grows thick with the cold smell of iron. A broken lantern chain trails
from the vault above, swaying a little in the draught.

213017.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

213017.description:
A long stretch of the Main Tunnel runs on here, its ceiling arched with
ribs of fitted stone that spring from corbels shaped like bearded heads.
Many of the faces have been chipped away, leaving blank, weeping scars.
Dust lies thick along the rock, but the middle of the road is scuffed
bare. North the passage meets a sharp bend, while south it runs toward a
broader, grander dark.

13018.name: A Bend In The Tunnel

east.description: To the east lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

13018.description:
The tunnel bends hard here, swinging from the long run coming up from
the south into a short reach that runs east. The walls are hewn rock,
scored with the long grooves of dwarven picks, and the floor is worn
into a shallow trough by generations of boots. An iron lamp-bracket,
long empty, hangs rusted at the corner. Cold air drifts along the bend,
carrying a smell of stone dust and old oil.

13019.name: A Bend In The Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

west.description: To the west lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

13019.description:
Here the tunnel turns again, the passage from the west curving up into a
straighter road that runs north. The ceiling lifts a little at the
corner, and the old masons left a ring of carved knotwork about the
keystone, its edges blurred by dust. A line of black soot streaks the
rock where lamps once burned. Your footfalls come back from the dark
with a hollow, patient echo.

13020.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies The Main Tunnel.

south.description: To the south lies A Bend In The Tunnel.

13020.description:
The Main Tunnel runs straight and broad here, wide enough for two ox-
carts to pass, its walls cut square and true from the living rock. Deep
ruts, worn by wheels long since gone, mark the floor. Rusted rings are
set into the rock at intervals, where beasts of burden were once
tethered. The road runs north toward a faint grey glow and falls away
south into dimness.

13021.name: The Main Tunnel

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Gate.

east.description: To the east lies Guardhouse.

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

13021.description:
The tunnel ends in a small squared chamber, where a heavy oak door
banded with iron stands in the east wall, scarred by old blows. To the
north the road opens out into Valin's Gate, its great arch just visible
in the gloom. Racks for spears and lanterns line the rock beside the
door, all of them bare. The air is fresher here, as if some far breath
of the outer world still reaches this far.

13022.name: Valin's Gate

south.description: To the south lies The Main Tunnel.

13022.description:
Valin's Gate rises as a vast arch of dressed grey stone, its twin leaves
of black iron shut and barred with a beam as thick as an old tree.
Dwarf-kings in relief march up either pillar, each holding an axe, their
faces worn smooth by the dust of centuries. Before the barred leaves
lies a paved forecourt, its flagstones cracked and heaped with drifted
grit. The only way out of this forlorn place is back along the tunnel to
the south.

extra_descs.kings relief pillar:
Carved on the pillars are eight dwarf-kings in procession, the foremost
bearing a key. Valin's name is cut beneath him, with the date of the
founding.

13023.name: Guardhouse

west.description: To the west lies The Main Tunnel.

13023.description:
The guardhouse is a long low room, its stone benches and pegged tables
left as if the watch had risen in the middle of a meal. A cold hearth
stands in one wall beneath a soot-blackened hood, and a rack of bent
halberd-heads rusts beside it. Narrow arrow slits look down on the
tunnel beyond. The only way out is the iron-banded door to the west,
back into the Main Tunnel.

13024.name: The Hall Of Splendor

east.description: To the east lies The Gate To The Stronghold.

up.description: To the up lies The Central Plaza.

13024.description:
Once the proudest audience hall of the city, the Hall of Splendor is a
forest of vast pillars carved as dwarf-kings, each bearing the vault
upon his shoulders. The mosaic floor shows a map of the old realm, now
cracked and pitted. A sweeping stair climbs up to the Central Plaza, and
the bronze-studded door to the east gives onto the Gate To The
Stronghold. Dust hangs in the air like fine smoke, lit by a dull glow
falling from above.

13025.name: The Central Plaza

north.description: To the north lies North Plaza.

east.description: To the east lies East Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies South Plaza.

west.description: To the west lies West Plaza.

down.description: To the down lies The Hall Of Splendor.

13025.description:
The Central Plaza spreads wide beneath the vast hollowed roof of the
mountain, paved with great flags of grey and rose stone laid in a
sunburst around a dry fountain. The basin is cracked, and the statue of
a dwarf at its centre has lost an arm and half a face. Broad ways lead
north, east, south and west to the other arms of the plaza, while a
stair goes down into the Hall of Splendor. Lamps on tall iron stands
burn here and there, leaving great pools of shadow between.

extra_descs.fountain statue basin:
The dry fountain is ringed with carved water-lilies, and its statue of a
dwarf holding a ladle has lost an arm. Dark stains in the basin show
where it once held water.

13026.name: Valin's Road

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Road.

south.description: To the south lies Valin's Road.

west.description: To the west lies A Nobles House.

13026.description:
The road continues here between rows of walled gardens, their rock-cut
beds long since overgrown with pale tangled roots. A gateway in the west
wall gives onto another noble house, its door ajar. A statue of a dwarf
lord lies in the road, toppled from its plinth and cracked in two.
Valin's Road runs on north and south.

13027.name: Valin's Road

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Road.

south.description: To the south lies Valin's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Baker's Guild.

13027.description:
The smell of long-dead ovens lingers about this stretch of Valin's Road,
where a broad doorway to the west leads to the Baker's Guild. A painted
wheatsheaf above the door has weathered to a brown smear. Spilled flour
has caked on the doorstep like dried plaster. The road runs on north and
south.

13028.name: The Baker's Guild

east.description: To the east lies Valin's Road.

13028.description:
The guild hall is dominated by a vast brick oven, big enough to bake a
hundred loaves at once, its iron door hanging open on a black mouth.
Long tables stand floured with the dust of years, and a wall of
pigeonholes holds the guild's rolls and seals. A bronze plaque lists the
masters of the craft. The door to the east leads back to Valin's Road.

13029.name: Valin's Road

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Road.

east.description: To the east lies The General Store.

south.description: To the south lies Valin's Road.

west.description: To the west lies A Nobles House.

13029.description:
This was once a busy junction of Valin's Road, where a shop opens to the
east and a gated house stands to the west. The paving is worn into a dip
in front of the General Store, where customers used to queue. Over the
house a canopy of carved stone leaves hangs, its edges chipped. Valin's
Road goes on both north and south from the junction.

13030.name: The General Store

west.description: To the west lies Valin's Road.

13030.description:
The general store is long and narrow, shelves stretching to the roof
beams and ladders on brass rails. Most shelves are bare, though a few
crates remain, nailed shut. A scale on the counter is clogged with rust,
and an old ledger lies open to a page of faded sums. The door to the
west leads out to Valin's Road.

13031.name: Valin's Road

north.description: To the north lies The Grand Stairs.

south.description: To the south lies Valin's Road.

west.description: To the west lies A Nobles House.

13031.description:
The road ends in a broad terrace before the Grand Stairs, which sweep
north into the lofty hall beyond, flanked by pillars carved as dwarf-
warriors. A noble house stands to the west behind a fence of black iron
spears. The terrace is littered with fragments of a smashed fountain.
The road runs back south.

13032.name: Bolgrim's Way

east.description: To the east lies Bolgrim's Way.

south.description: To the south lies Eryn's Road.

west.description: To the west lies Bolgrim's Way.

13032.description:
Bolgrim's Way begins as a smooth road of black basalt setts, running
beneath a ceiling hung with the soot of ten thousand lamps. A lamp-post
of beaten iron stands at the corner, its glass long shattered. The walls
of the rich quarter rise on either hand, windowless and proud. South the
way meets Eryn's Road, while the Way itself runs east toward a squat
tower and west toward the jewellers' houses.

13033.name: Bolgrim's Way

east.description: To the east lies Bolgrim's Way.

south.description: To the south lies Buccia's Alley.

west.description: To the west lies The Grand Stairs.

13033.description:
Bolgrim's Way begins at the foot of the Grand Stairs, whose pale marble
flanks the road to the west. A narrow door in the south wall, half
hidden by a drooping canopy, leads into Buccia's Alley. The paving is
laid with river-pebbles brought long ago from the surface. The Way runs
on east toward the jewellers.

13034.name: Bolgrim's Way

north.description: To the north lies The House Of Gems.

east.description: To the east lies Bolgrim's Way.

west.description: To the west lies Bolgrim's Way.

13034.description:
A glass-fronted house of white stone stands on the north side, its
lintel carved with faceted gems: the House of Gems. Its windows are
shuttered with iron grilles, and a stone dwarf in armour stands on each
side of the door. Bolgrim's Way continues east toward a crossroad and
west toward the stairs.

13035.name: The House Of Gems

south.description: To the south lies Bolgrim's Way.

13035.description:
The jeweller's showroom has glass-topped cases set along its walls,
empty save for scraps of velvet. A chandelier of cut crystal hangs from
the ceiling, dull with dust. Mirrors behind the counter have clouded to
the colour of pewter. The way out is south, onto Bolgrim's Way.

13036.name: Bolgrim's Way

east.description: To the east lies Bolgrim's Way.

south.description: To the south lies Theo's Magical Things.

west.description: To the west lies Bolgrim's Way.

13036.description:
Fine shopfronts line this stretch of Bolgrim's Way, their glass long
gone and their shutters hanging by one hinge. A signboard painted with a
star and a wand sways over a doorway to the south, announcing Theo's
Magical Things. The cobbles are patched with slabs of different stone,
as though the street had been mended in haste, again and again. The Way
runs on east and west.

13037.name: Bolgrim's Way

north.description: To the north lies A Private Home.

east.description: To the east lies Before The Watchtower.

west.description: To the west lies Bolgrim's Way.

13037.description:
A narrow house with a door of dark wood stands to the north, set back
behind a worn step and a pair of stone urns that hold only dead roots.
Bolgrim's Way continues east toward a squat tower and west back along
the shopfronts. The paving is clean here, swept recently, which is
strange in so neglected a street. Carved vines climb the pillars on
either side of the house door.

13038.name: Before The Watchtower

east.description: To the east lies A Guard Room.

south.description: To the south lies Fain's Highway.

west.description: To the west lies Bolgrim's Way.

13038.description:
The road widens into a cobbled yard before the watchtower, whose walls
of grey stone rise straight up to the roof of the mountain. A heavy door
to the east stands ajar, the entrance to the guard room, and a worn
mounting-block squats beside it. Bolgrim's Way comes in from the west,
and Fain's Highway leaves south along a gentler slope. Scorch marks
blacken the cobbles, souvenirs of some old fight.

13039.name: A Guard Room

west.description: To the west lies Before The Watchtower.

up.description: To the up lies The Iron Staircase.

13039.description:
The guard room is cramped and smoky, with a squat iron stove, a rack of
dented shields on one wall, and a table pitted by dagger points. Maps of
the city's tunnels are pinned up, curling and brown. A stair of iron
spirals upward through a hole in the ceiling, ringing faintly whenever
the draught stirs. The door to the west opens onto the yard before the
watchtower.

13041.name: The Iron Staircase

up.description: To the up lies At The Top Of The Watchtower.

down.description: To the down lies A Guard Room.

13041.description:
The iron staircase winds in a tight spiral inside the watchtower's
shaft, each step a perforated plate that shows glimpses of the dark
below. The handrail is cold and pitted with rust, and the whole
structure hums softly under any weight. Arrow slits cut through the
thick wall at each turn let in thin bars of grey light. The stair leads
up to the top of the tower and down to the guard room.

13042.name: At The Top Of The Watchtower

down.description: To the down lies The Iron Staircase.

13042.description:
The watchtower's summit is a round platform of fitted stone, ringed by a
crenellated parapet that overlooks the whole upper city. From here the
Central Plaza looks like a dim coin, and the dark roads below are strung
with the occasional lamp. A great iron brazier, long cold, holds a drift
of grey ash, and the cracked signal-horn mounted beside it has not
sounded for years. The only way down is the iron stair.

13043.name: Fain's Highway

north.description: To the north lies Before The Watchtower.

east.description: To the east lies A Private Home.

south.description: To the south lies Fain's Highway.

13043.description:
Fain's Highway starts here as a wide thoroughfare running away from the
watchtower, its centre line marked by a strip of bronze studs worn
bright by wheels. A door of dark oak on the east side opens into a
private home, its brass knocker shaped like a dwarf's fist. Gutters run
along either kerb, choked with the black mud of years. The highway goes
north to the watchtower yard and south along the tunnel city.

13044.name: Fain's Highway

north.description: To the north lies Fain's Highway.

south.description: To the south lies Fain's Highway.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark Alley.

13044.description:
A dark alley mouths on the west side of the highway here, a slot of deep
shadow between two blank-walled warehouses. The highway itself is lit by
a pair of wall-lamps burning a sullen yellow, the only ones still tended
in this stretch. Stains and scrapes on the paving tell of fights that
were never reported. North the highway runs back toward the watchtower,
and south it descends the slope.

13045.name: Fain's Highway

north.description: To the north lies Fain's Highway.

east.description: To the east lies An Abandon House.

south.description: To the south lies Fain's Highway.

13045.description:
The door of an abandoned house stands crooked on its hinges to the east,
its lintel marked with a chalk cross, the old sign that none live
within. Pale fungus pushes up between the cobbles at the foot of the
wall. Across the highway a row of iron hitching posts leans like drunks
at closing time. Fain's Highway runs on north and south.

13046.name: Fain's Highway

north.description: To the north lies Fain's Highway.

east.description: To the east lies The Hall Of Weaponry.

south.description: To the south lies Fain's Highway.

13046.description:
A broad archway of polished granite marks the entrance to the Hall of
Weaponry on the east side, carved with crossed axes and a battle-scene
in shallow relief. Shop-signs of other trades hang rusted from brackets
up and down the highway. The paving is smoother here, laid by better
masons than those who built the rest. Fain's Highway continues north and
south.

13047.name: Fain's Highway

north.description: To the north lies Fain's Highway.

east.description: To the east lies An Abandon House.

south.description: To the south lies Fain's Highway.

west.description: To the west lies Durgar's Street.

13047.description:
Fain's Highway meets Durgar's Street here at a rough crossing, the
cross-street running away west toward the plaza. On the east side, a
boarded door under a rotted lintel marks another abandoned house. A
milestone at the corner, carved as a seated dwarf with a beard to his
knees, gives distances in a script few can read now. The highway runs on
north and south.

extra_descs.milestone dwarf seated:
The milestone is cut as a seated dwarf with his hands on his knees, and
the distances to the gates and the mines are scored down his beard in
rune-script. Someone has scratched out the figure for the stronghold and
cut a crown in its place.

13048.name: Fain's Highway

north.description: To the north lies Fain's Highway.

south.description: To the south lies Fain's Highway.

west.description: To the west lies Helm's Armory.

13048.description:
Helm's Armory squats to the west in a stout building of riveted iron
plates, a great shield of beaten bronze hanging over its door. The
sounds of the street are dulled here, as if the heavy walls swallowed
them. Deep wheel-ruts in the paving show where armour carts once made
their deliveries. North and south the highway goes on.

13049.name: Fain's Highway

north.description: To the north lies Fain's Highway.

east.description: To the east lies An Abandon House.

south.description: To the south lies The Mining District.

13049.description:
The highway slopes down toward the mining district, and the air grows
heavy with the smell of coal-smoke and hot metal. An abandoned house
stands to the east with its windows gaping like missing teeth. Grit and
slag have been tracked up the road on miners' boots, and the paving here
is black. The highway leads north back up the slope, and south into the
Mining District.

13050.name: The Mining District

north.description: To the north lies Fain's Highway.

west.description: To the west lies Bard's Street.

13050.description:
Black slag heaps rise on every side, and the walls are streaked with the
rust and soot of the ore-smelters that once roared here. Rails of
rotting timber cross the floor where carts of ore once rolled between
the workings, and a great cracked bellows hangs from a gantry overhead.
The air tastes of old coal and iron. The highway climbs north, while
Bard's Street leads off west along the face of the diggings.

13051.name: Bard's Street

east.description: To the east lies The Mining District.

south.description: To the south lies The Corner Store.

west.description: To the west lies Bard's Street.

13051.description:
Bard's Street begins here, lined with low, soot-grimed shops and
tenements whose upper floors lean out until they almost touch overhead.
A door to the south, under a painted sign of a barrel and a loaf,
belongs to the Corner Store. The cobbles are black and slippery, and the
gutter runs with a thin trickle of grey water. The street runs east to
the Mining District and west along the tenements.

13052.name: Bard's Street

east.description: To the east lies Bard's Street.

west.description: To the west lies Bard's Street.

13052.description:
The tenements press close on both sides here, their stairwells open to
the street and reeking of damp. Strings of dead lanterns are slung from
window to window, and a shrine to some forgotten dwarf-saint is cut into
the wall at head height, its candle-cup empty. A battered cart-wheel
leans against a doorway. Bard's Street runs on east and west.

13053.name: Bard's Street

north.description: To the north lies Eryn's Road.

east.description: To the east lies Bard's Street.

west.description: To the west lies Bard's Street.

13053.description:
A crossing where Eryn's Road comes in from the north and Bard's Street
runs on east and west. The corner building has a shop front of iron
grilles, now locked, and its doorstep is worn into a shallow dish by
many feet. A stone trough stands at the crossing, dry and green with old
slime. Faint voices from the plaza sometimes echo down the road from the
north, and are gone.

13054.name: Bard's Street

north.description: To the north lies The Mineral Storage.

east.description: To the east lies Bard's Street.

west.description: To the west lies Bard's Street.

13054.description:
Bard's Street ends in a stretch of loading bays, and a heavy door of
iron-bound planks to the north leads into the mineral storage. Rusty
streaks stain the ground below a crane-arm hung with frayed chains. The
street runs east toward Eryn's Road and west toward the miners' halls. A
single lamp over the door burns a dim, steady blue.

13055.name: Bard's Street

north.description: To the north lies Miner's Hall.

east.description: To the east lies Bard's Street.

west.description: To the west lies The Mining District.

13055.description:
Bard's Street is lined here with the narrow doors of miners' lodgings,
row on row, each with a chalked number faded to a ghost. A wide double
door in the north wall, painted with a pair of crossed picks, is the
entrance to the Miner's Hall. Boots have worn its step to a smooth
hollow. Bard's Street runs east, and west toward the square of the
Mining District.

13056.name: The Mining District

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Road.

east.description: To the east lies Bard's Street.

13056.description:
The heart of the mining quarter is a ragged square of trampled slag,
ringed by sheds and pit-head frames, where the diggers once gathered at
the shift-bell. A rusted bell hangs from a timber gantry, its clapper
gone. Water drips from a split spout into a trough stained orange.
Valin's Road climbs away north, and Bard's Street leads off east between
the lodgings.

13057.name: Valin's Road

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Mining District.

13057.description:
The road narrows and slopes downward, the pale stone of the nobles'
quarter turning to rough grey flags blackened with soot. Gouges left by
iron-shod wheels score the paving in deep parallel lines. A leaning
signpost with its arms snapped off stands at the edge of the road, its
lettering scoured away. Valin's Road climbs back north, while to the
south the air thickens with the taste of smoke.

13058.name: Valin's Road

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Road.

south.description: To the south lies Valin's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Residence Of Lord Brute.

13058.description:
Valin's Road dips here toward the working quarter, the fine paving of
the nobles' houses giving way to plain flags rutted by heavy cart-
wheels. A door of thick planks to the west bears the iron-bound crest of
Lord Brute, a boar's head above crossed picks. Soot has begun to stain
the walls and the lamp-standards. The road runs north toward the great
houses and south toward the diggings.

13059.name: Valin's Road

north.description: To the north lies Valin's Road.

east.description: To the east lies Durgar's Street.

south.description: To the south lies Valin's Road.

west.description: To the west lies A Nobles House.

13059.description:
Valin's Road is a handsome thoroughfare of pale paving, running between
the walls of the great houses. A door of carved cedar to the west
belongs to a noble family now vanished, and the golden anvil of its
crest is flaking. The road runs north up a gentle ramp, south toward the
workings, and east to join Durgar's Street. Ornate lamp-standards line
the roadway, every one of them dark.

13060.name: The Grand Stairs

east.description: To the east lies Bolgrim's Way.

south.description: To the south lies Valin's Road.

up.description: To the up lies At The End Of A Long Hallway.

13060.description:
The Grand Stairs rise in a magnificent sweep of white marble, wide
enough for twenty dwarves abreast, though the stone is cracked and
stained with black. At the head of the flight the way up stands open, a
tall archway giving onto the upper halls, no longer barred. A passage
leads east onto Bolgrim's Way, and the terrace outside lies south. A
carved balustrade follows the stairs, its newel posts shaped like
crowned lions.

13061.name: North Plaza

north.description: To the north lies Eryn's Road.

east.description: To the east lies Northeast Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies The Central Plaza.

west.description: To the west lies Northwest Plaza.

13061.description:
This arm of the plaza is lined with the shuttered fronts of old guild
halls, their lintels carved with hammers, anvils and scales. The
pavement is stained dark in long lines where water ran from broken
gutters. A road leaves north as Eryn's Road, and the open paving goes on
east, south and west to the rest of the plaza. A banner pole stands bare
in the middle of the flags, its rope swaying against it in the draught.

13062.name: Northeast Plaza

south.description: To the south lies East Plaza.

west.description: To the west lies North Plaza.

13062.description:
This corner of the plaza is closed in by a collapsed arcade whose rubble
spills across the flags in a fan of broken columns. A tall stone clock
stands against the wall, its face gone black and its hands snapped off
at the hour of some forgotten disaster. Dwarf-runes ring the dial. The
plaza continues west to the North Plaza and south to the East Plaza.

13063.name: East Plaza

north.description: To the north lies Northeast Plaza.

east.description: To the east lies Durgar's Street.

south.description: To the south lies Southeast Plaza.

west.description: To the west lies The Central Plaza.

13063.description:
The plaza's east edge is marked by a long low wall topped with iron
spikes, behind which gardens of pale stone mushrooms once grew. Traders'
pitches are scratched out in white on the paving, worn almost invisible.
Durgar's Street leaves east through a gap in the wall. The plaza goes on
north and south, and west to its centre.

13064.name: Southeast Plaza

north.description: To the north lies East Plaza.

west.description: To the west lies South Plaza.

13064.description:
The plaza ends in a corner here, where two walls of carved stone meet in
a point and a bench has been built into the angle. The carvings show a
procession of craftsmen bearing the tools of their trades, and each has
a different face. Lamplight is poor, and the corner is full of shifting
shadow. The paving leads north to the East Plaza and west along the
South Plaza.

13065.name: South Plaza

north.description: To the north lies The Central Plaza.

east.description: To the east lies Southeast Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies Eryn's Road.

west.description: To the west lies Southwest Plaza.

13065.description:
The south arm of the plaza is a wide apron of paving, bounded by the
dark arches of a colonnade whose pillars are carved like bundled axe-
hafts. Ash-grey dust lies in drifts against the base of each column. A
rusty iron lamp-standard leans at an angle, its crown of glass long
gone. The plaza spreads on to the north, east and west, and Eryn's Road
leaves to the south.

13066.name: Southwest Plaza

north.description: To the north lies West Plaza.

east.description: To the east lies South Plaza.

13066.description:
A quiet corner of the plaza, where a bronze plaque set in the paving
lists the names of the city's founders, half of them worn to nothing. A
stone bench faces a wall of reliefs showing the first digging of the
mountain. The lamps here have been unlit so long that their wicks have
turned to stone. The plaza runs north to the West Plaza and east to the
South Plaza.

13067.name: West Plaza

north.description: To the north lies Northwest Plaza.

east.description: To the east lies The Central Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies Southwest Plaza.

west.description: To the west lies Durgar's Street.

13067.description:
The plaza's west edge opens onto Durgar's Street through a high gateway,
its keystone carved with an anvil and a crown. A row of stone benches
stands under a colonnade, their seats broken and furred with pale
lichen. Light from distant lamps barely reaches the corners. The plaza
goes on north and south, and east to its centre.

13068.name: Northwest Plaza

north.description: To the north lies Lord Stern's Mansion.

east.description: To the east lies North Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies West Plaza.

13068.description:
A tall house-front of rose-coloured stone rises to the north, its great
double door topped with a carved stag's head, the mansion of Lord Stern.
Iron railings enclose a forecourt of dead ornamental shrubs. The paving
is swept clean in a path to the door, while elsewhere it lies thick with
dust. The plaza runs east to the North Plaza and south to the West
Plaza.

13069.name: Durgar's Street

north.description: To the north lies The Market Hall.

east.description: To the east lies Fain's Highway.

south.description: To the south lies The Old Bell Tavern.

west.description: To the west lies East Plaza.

13069.description:
Durgar's Street is a handsome avenue wide enough for a marching column,
its flagstones laid in long bands of grey and ochre. Hanging signs on
the north side advertise the Market Hall, while a creaking sign shaped
like a brass bell marks the tavern to the south. The street runs east
toward Fain's Highway and west to the plaza. Blackened lamp-brackets jut
from every second pillar.

13070.name: The Market Hall

south.description: To the south lies Durgar's Street.

13070.description:
The market hall is a high stone barn of a room, its stalls ranged in
orderly rows beneath a ceiling of painted beams that show the seasons of
the world above. Most stalls are bare boards on trestles, though a few
still carry faded awnings and counting-slates. Dust sits on everything
in an even grey blanket. The only door is on the south side, onto
Durgar's Street.

13071.name: The Old Bell Tavern

north.description: To the north lies Durgar's Street.

13071.description:
A big square taproom with a low beamed ceiling and a great hearth, where
a huge bronze bell hangs above the bar and rings faintly when the
draught moves. Long tables of black oak, scarred by generations of mugs,
fill the floor, and the benches are worn pale by sitting. The smell of
old ale has soaked into the very walls. The door north leads out to
Durgar's Street.

13072.name: Durgar's Street

north.description: To the north lies The Ruby Inn.

east.description: To the east lies West Plaza.

south.description: To the south lies Clem's Bank.

west.description: To the west lies Valin's Road.

13072.description:
Durgar's Street meets Valin's Road here in a wide junction, and a carved
stone wellhead stands in the middle, its windlass long gone. The Ruby
Inn lies to the north behind a window of red glass, and the vault-door
of Clem's Bank squats to the south. The street continues east toward the
plaza, and Valin's Road runs away west. A bar of pale light from a high
shaft falls across the wellhead.

13073.name: The Ruby Inn

south.description: To the south lies Durgar's Street.

west.description: To the west lies Common Room.

13073.description:
The Ruby Inn's entrance hall glows dull crimson from windows of red
glass, and a long polished counter of dark wood runs along one wall. A
stair climbs up to the reception rooms above, and an archway on the west
side opens on the common room. The floor is strewn with rushes gone
brittle and brown, and the lamps are unlit. The street door is south.

13074.name: Common Room

east.description: To the east lies The Ruby Inn.

13074.description:
A long, low common room with a fireplace big enough to roast an ox, now
cold. Dozens of mismatched stools and benches are pushed against the
walls, and a dartboard of pitted wood hangs askew. A mural of dwarves at
a feast has been half washed away by seepage. The only way out is the
archway to the east.

13075.name: Reception

down.description: To the down lies The Ruby Inn.

13075.description:
A quiet upper chamber with a writing desk, a bell-pull of tarnished
velvet, and a ledger the size of a paving slab chained to the counter.
Faded portraits of the inn's owners watch from the walls, their eyes
mostly scratched out. The air is stuffy and smells of old paper. A stair
leads down to the lobby of the Ruby Inn.

13076.name: Clem's Bank

north.description: To the north lies Durgar's Street.

13076.description:
A vault of grey stone, its walls lined with iron-bound strongboxes that
stand open and empty. A heavy teller's counter is guarded by thick brass
bars, and a great scale hangs over it, its pans bent. The ceiling bears
a mosaic of coins and a laughing dwarf with a ledger. The only way out
is north, onto Durgar's Street.

13077.name: Eryn's Road

north.description: To the north lies Eryn's Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Cityguard's Headquarters.

south.description: To the south lies North Plaza.

13077.description:
Eryn's Road begins here, a broad paved way between tall townhouses with
carved stone balconies, most of them dark. The cobbles are set in a
herringbone of grey and rust-red, though many have sunk or been prised
out. To the east stands the squat, heavily barred Cityguard's
Headquarters, its door yawning open. North the road continues up the
street, and south it opens onto the plaza.

13078.name: Eryn's Road

north.description: To the north lies Eryn's Road.

east.description: To the east lies A Dark Alley.

south.description: To the south lies Eryn's Road.

west.description: To the west lies Guards Barracks.

13078.description:
A cramped crossing on Eryn's Road, where a narrow dark alley slips away
east between two leaning houses, and a heavy-timbered doorway to the
west opens on the Guards Barracks. Old oil lamps hang from iron arms
over the street, rusted and unlit. A drain grating in the middle of the
road gurgles faintly. The road runs on north and south from the
crossing.

13079.name: Eryn's Road

north.description: To the north lies Bolgrim's Way.

south.description: To the south lies Eryn's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Prison.

13079.description:
The road narrows here between blank walls of dressed stone, and a squat,
grim building to the west shows a barred door, the city prison. Iron-
shod posts along the kerb carry hanging chains where prisoners were once
led. The paving is greasy with old soot. North the road meets Bolgrim's
Way, and south it runs back toward the plaza.

13080.name: Eryn's Road

north.description: To the north lies South Plaza.

east.description: To the east lies The Cartographers.

south.description: To the south lies Bard's Street.

13080.description:
Eryn's Road ends in a short paved approach to the plaza, which glimmers
dimly ahead to the north. The Cartographers' house stands to the east,
its door set with a brass plate engraved with a compass, tarnished
green. The road is clean and well swept here, as though the guild still
cared about its doorstep. South the road meets Bard's Street.

13081.name: The Cityguard's Headquarters

north.description: To the north lies The Officers Room.

east.description: To the east lies The Sleeping Quarters.

west.description: To the west lies Eryn's Road.

13081.description:
The headquarters is a stone hall with a long counter, a notice board of
curling bills, and a wall-map of the city bristling with pins. A brazier
stands cold in the middle of the floor. Doors lead north to the
officers' room and east to the sleeping quarters. The street lies to the
west.

13082.name: The Officers Room

south.description: To the south lies The Cityguard's Headquarters.

13082.description:
A tidy room with a brass-bound desk, a map table, and a rack of
ceremonial halberds standing in the corner. A hat-stand holds a
captain's plumed helm under a coat of dust. The window is just a slit
onto an airshaft. The only door leads south into the headquarters.

13083.name: The Sleeping Quarters

west.description: To the west lies The Cityguard's Headquarters.

13083.description:
Cots stand in rows under a low vaulted ceiling, blankets folded at their
feet, a cold stove squatting in the middle of the room. The air is stale
with years of sleeping soldiers. A single lantern hangs unlit from a
hook above the door. The only way out is west, into the headquarters.

13084.name: Guards Barracks

east.description: To the east lies Eryn's Road.

13084.description:
Rows of bunks line the walls of the barracks, each with a footlocker and
a grey blanket tucked tight. Pegs hold the shadows of armour that no
longer hangs there, and a long table in the middle carries the ring-
marks of many mugs. A regimental pennant, black with soot, droops from a
pole. The only exit is the door to the east, onto Eryn's Road.

13085.name: The Prison

east.description: To the east lies Eryn's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Prison Cell.

13085.description:
The prison is a squat guardroom of grey stone, with a table scarred by
knives and a rack of iron keys hanging on hooks. Manacles are bolted to
a post in the middle of the floor. A heavy iron door in the west wall
leads to the cell beyond, and the street lies to the east. The air is
sour with damp and old sweat.

13086.name: The Prison Cell

east.description: To the east lies The Prison.

13086.description:
A tiny cell, a bare stone floor and a rock shelf for a bed, with iron
staples in the wall where chains once hung. Scratched tallies cover one
wall in uneven rows of five. A narrow barred slit lets in a sliver of
dim lamplight. The iron door to the east opens onto the prison.

13087.name: A Dark Alley

east.description: To the east lies A Dark Alley.

west.description: To the west lies Eryn's Road.

13087.description:
The alley mouth opens west onto Eryn's Road, a dim rectangle of
lamplight at the end of the passage. The walls are sooty, scrawled over
with thieves' marks and tally-lines. A drain runs down the middle,
clogged with old rubbish. The alley goes on east, deeper into the dark.

13088.name: A Dark Alley

east.description: To the east lies Fain's Highway.

south.description: To the south lies The Shop Of Small And Wondrous Things.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark Alley.

13088.description:
Darkness crowds this stretch of the alley, and the walls lean in from
both sides until the ceiling of the mountain is lost above. A thread of
green light shows beneath a door in the south wall, the entrance to the
Shop Of Small And Wondrous Things. Puddles of black water lie between
the cobbles. The alley runs east toward Fain's Highway and west into
deeper shadow.

13089.name: The Shop Of Small And Wondrous Things

north.description: To the north lies A Dark Alley.

13089.description:
Shelves and glass cases crowd every wall of this narrow shop, crammed
with curiosities and oddments of brass and glass. A clockwork bird
perches on the counter, its wings frozen halfway through a beat. Lamps
of coloured glass cast a mottled light on the ceiling. The way out is
north, into the alley.

13090.name: Miner's Hall

north.description: To the north lies The Shaft.

south.description: To the south lies Bard's Street.

west.description: To the west lies The Miner's Office.

13090.description:
A low timbered hall where the miners' guild once held its meetings and
paid out wages at a long counter. Benches are ranged along the walls,
and the pay-window is shuttered with an iron grille. A door in the north
wall, black with grease, leads to the shaft-head, and an opening to the
west gives onto the guild office. The street entrance stands to the
south.

13091.name: The Shaft

south.description: To the south lies Miner's Hall.

down.description: To the down lies The Entrance To The Mines.

13091.description:
A square pit-head built of massive timbers, with the great wheel of a
winding-gear overhead, its rope long since rotted away. The floor is a
platform of planks laid around a black opening, from which a cold breath
rises with a smell of wet stone. The gate that once locked the way down
has been thrown wide, and iron rungs lead into the darkness. The door
south leads back to the hall.

extra_descs.gate rungs opening:
The iron gate hangs from one hinge, and its lock has been cut through.
The rungs below it are worn bright in the middle, as if used often and
lately.

13092.name: The Miner's Office

east.description: To the east lies Miner's Hall.

13092.description:
A cramped office with a slanted drafting desk, pigeonholes stuffed with
survey scrolls, and a wall-map of the galleries inked in a careful,
faded hand. Red lines mark the seams that were richest, and black
crosses mark the places where roofs fell in. A stub of candle has melted
into a saucer. The only way out is the opening east, into the hall.

13093.name: The Hall Of Weaponry

west.description: To the west lies Fain's Highway.

13093.description:
Long racks line the walls of this lofty hall, mostly bare now, with only
the outlines of what once hung there picked out in clean stone behind
them. A forge-hearth in the corner is cold, and the great stone anvil
beside it is dented by countless blows. The vaulted ceiling is stained
with the smoke of generations of smiths. The archway on the west side
leads back to Fain's Highway.

13094.name: Helm's Armory

east.description: To the east lies Fain's Highway.

13094.description:
The armory smells of cold iron and oil. Rows of empty stands shaped like
dwarves with raised arms line the walls, awaiting plate that was sold
off or stolen. A great bellows hangs over a forge-pit and a pair of
tongs lies rusting on the anvil. The door to the east leads out to
Fain's Highway.

13095.name: Theo's Magical Things

north.description: To the north lies Bolgrim's Way.

13095.description:
A wizard's shop of crooked shelves, the floor scrawled with sigils in
white chalk and a brazier of violet embers burning cold in one corner.
Strings of dried herbs and bundles of feathers hang from the rafters.
The shop sign swings above the door with a faint squeak. The door in the
north wall leads back out to Bolgrim's Way.

13096.name: The Mineral Storage

south.description: To the south lies Bard's Street.

13096.description:
A long warehouse of stone bays, each one heaped with spilled chips of
coloured rock: green, ochre, grey-blue. Scales hang on iron arms over
every bay, and sorting-tables stand nearby, riddled with the pits of
countless hammer-blows. The air tastes of dust. The door to the south
leads out to Bard's Street.

13097.name: The Residence Of Lord Brute

east.description: To the east lies Valin's Road.

13097.description:
The residence of Lord Brute is a fortress of a house, its hall hung with
the tusked heads of boars and the shields of defeated rivals. A great
chair of black iron stands on a dais, its arms worn bright by a heavy
hand. The floor is scored with the scrapes of dragged furniture, as if
the household left in a hurry. The door in the east wall opens on
Valin's Road.

13098.name: A Private Home

west.description: To the west lies Fain's Highway.

13098.description:
A tidy dwarven parlour with a low ceiling of dark beams, where an iron
kettle hangs over a cold hearth and a faded rug lies before it. Shelves
along one wall hold crocks and a few leather-bound ledgers. Chalk tally
marks on the mantel record some forgotten household reckoning. The only
way out is the door to the west, onto Fain's Highway.

13099.name: A Private Home

south.description: To the south lies Bolgrim's Way.

13099.description:
This is the front room of a modest dwarven house, snug and low-beamed,
with a hearth swept clean and a heavy table scarred by long years of
meals. Pegs on the wall hold a few threadbare cloaks, and a shuttered
window lets in a thin slant of lamplight from the street. Blankets lie
folded on a bench by the fire. The door to the south leads back out onto
Bolgrim's Way.

13100.name: A Nobles House

east.description: To the east lies Valin's Road.

13100.description:
The hall of a once-grand house, its floor of black and white tile now
cracked, and its walls hung with the pale ghosts of vanished paintings.
A chandelier of rusted iron lies in a heap in the middle of the room,
where its chain gave way. Gilded door-frames hang open on empty rooms.
The great door in the east wall leads out to Valin's Road.

13101.name: A Nobles House

east.description: To the east lies Valin's Road.

13101.description:
A drawing room with a hearth of carved marble and a pair of high-backed
chairs, their upholstery eaten to the stuffing. Heavy curtains of green
velvet hang rotting from their rods. A harp with a few snapped strings
leans in the corner, gathering dust. The door in the east wall leads
back to Valin's Road.

13102.name: A Nobles House

east.description: To the east lies Valin's Road.

13102.description:
A long dining hall, its table a single slab of grey granite ringed with
high-backed chairs of black wood. Silver candle-stands, green with
tarnish, still march down the middle of the board, each stub of wax
burned to a puddle. Tapestries of a boar hunt hang in rags from the
walls, and the hearth is choked with old soot. The door in the east wall
leads back out to Valin's Road.

13103.name: A Nobles House

east.description: To the east lies Valin's Road.

13103.description:
A noble bedchamber, its great bed canopied in dust-grey brocade, and its
wardrobe doors hanging open on empty hooks. A dressing-table holds a
cracked mirror and a dried-up pot of paint. Over the mantel hangs a
portrait of a stern dwarf lady, her face slashed by some vandal. The
door to the east leads out to Valin's Road.

13104.name: An Abandon House

west.description: To the west lies Fain's Highway.

13104.description:
Dust lies over everything in this house, thick enough to show a single
line of prints crossing the floor from door to hearth. Chairs are
overturned, a cupboard hangs open, and plaster has fallen in grey lumps
from the ceiling. A cold fireplace gapes in the far wall, a few charred
sticks still in the grate. The door to the west lets in a thin lamp-glow
from the highway.

13105.name: An Abandon House

west.description: To the west lies Fain's Highway.

13105.description:
A long-empty house, its shutters nailed across the windows and its door
hanging by a single strap of leather. In the main room the furniture has
been dragged into a heap in one corner, and a moth-eaten tapestry sags
on its rod. Fine pale roots of some fungus have lifted several
flagstones. The way out is back through the door to the west.

13106.name: An Abandon House

west.description: To the west lies Fain's Highway.

13106.description:
The third of the empty houses along this stretch has fared worst: the
roof has partly caved, and a heap of fallen stone fills one corner of
the room. A faded mural of a bear-hunt covers the one wall still sound,
blistered with damp. A draught whines through a crack in the ceiling.
The door to the west is the only way out.

13107.name: Lord Stern's Mansion

south.description: To the south lies Northwest Plaza.

13107.description:
Lord Stern's hall is vast and hung with moth-eaten banners of crimson
and gold, beneath a vault painted with the deeds of his forefathers. A
long table of polished black stone runs the length of the floor, set for
a feast that no one has come to eat. A gallery runs along the far wall,
its balustrade broken in several places. The only door leads south onto
the plaza.

13108.name: The Cartographers

west.description: To the west lies Eryn's Road.

13108.description:
The cartographers' workshop is lined with sloping tables, where yellowed
maps of the roads and tunnels are pinned down by lead weights. A great
painted globe of the underworld stands in the corner, its lower half
cracked. Brass compasses and dividers hang on the walls, dull with age.
The door to the west opens on Eryn's Road.

13109.name: The Corner Store

north.description: To the north lies Bard's Street.

13109.description:
A cramped little shop, its counter scarred and its shelves mostly empty,
with only a few jars and crocks lined up at the back. The ceiling is
hung with iron hooks that once held smoked fish and sausage. A lantern
on a chain gives a feeble, wavering light. The door to the north opens
onto Bard's Street.

13110.name: Buccia's Alley

north.description: To the north lies Bolgrim's Way.

south.description: To the south lies A Slight Bend In The Alleyway.

13110.description:
A cramped alley slopes down between the high backs of mansions, its
cobbles slick with seepage. Tangles of wire and old rope hang between
the walls, strung with the remnants of washing lines. The only light
comes from a shuttered lamp at the head of the alley. The alley winds
south and opens north onto Bolgrim's Way.

13111.name: A Slight Bend In The Alleyway

north.description: To the north lies Buccia's Alley.

east.description: To the east lies Buccia's Alley.

13111.description:
A slight bend in the alley, where the walls lean toward each other until
they almost meet overhead. A stone drain runs down the centre, gurgling
faintly. Chalked arrows on the wall point the ways out, and beside them
is a word in an unreadable hand. The alley goes north toward its head
and east to a longer stretch.

13112.name: Buccia's Alley

south.description: To the south lies The Golden Plough.

west.description: To the west lies A Slight Bend In The Alleyway.

13112.description:
The alley runs along the back of a long building, and a smell of stale
beer and frying grease drifts from an open arch to the south, the way
into the Golden Plough. Barrel staves and broken crates are stacked
against the wall. A hanging lamp in an iron cage gives a weak orange
glow. The alley turns back west.

13113.name: The Golden Plough

north.description: To the north lies Buccia's Alley.

south.description: To the south lies The Back Room.

13113.description:
The Golden Plough is a noisy tavern room gone silent, with a great wheel
of a plough hung above the hearth and its brass long tarnished. Tables
are heaped with upturned stools, and a counter of scarred oak is lit by
a single guttering lamp. A heavy door in the south wall leads to the
back room. The alley lies north.

13114.name: The Back Room

north.description: To the north lies The Golden Plough.

down.description: To the down lies Below The Tavern.

13114.description:
A windowless back room, with a rough table, a rack of casks, and a
trapdoor in the floor that stands wide open on a ladder of cold iron. A
draught of mineral-scented air rises from the dark below. The wall is
scratched with tally-marks and the initials of smugglers. The door north
leads back to the tavern.

650300.name: dwarf citizen townsman
650300.long_desc: A gaunt dwarf citizen hurries past, hugging a worn cloak and glancing at the shadows.
650300.description:
A short, broad dwarf with a greying beard braided in mourning knots. His
coat was fine once, but is darned and patched at the elbows, and he eyes
you with wary, tired courtesy.

650301.name: renegade dwarf guard soldier
650301.long_desc: A renegade dwarf guard stands watch with a notched axe, his livery stripped of the city's crest.
650301.description:
The dwarf wears the grey tabard of the city watch, the crest torn off
and replaced with a crude crown daubed in red. His helm is dented, his
eyes hard, and he grips his axe like a man who has already chosen a
side.

650302.name: pale tunnel spider
650302.long_desc: A pale tunnel spider clings to the rock overhead, its many eyes catching the lamplight.
650302.description:
The spider is as big as a wolf, bloated and bone-white from a life
without light. Its legs end in hooked claws that rasp on the stone, and
thick strands of grey silk trail from its spinnerets.

650303.name: stone golem guardian
650303.long_desc: A hulking stone golem stands motionless among the pillars, until it turns its blank face toward you.
650303.description:
The golem is hewn from a single block of grey granite, carved in the
likeness of a dwarf in plate armour. Rune-lines glow dull orange in its
chest, and each slow step shakes dust from the vault above.

650304.name: usurper champion dwarf warrior
650304.long_desc: The usurper's champion paces the tunnel in black plate, a warhammer resting on his shoulder.
650304.description:
A massive dwarf in blackened plate, his beard bound in iron rings and
his face scarred across both cheeks. He bears a crown stamped in red wax
upon his breastplate and swings a warhammer as easily as a walking
stick.

650305.name: lord stern turncloak noble dwarf
650305.long_desc: Lord Stern the Turncloak sits at his long table in crimson and gold, a drawn blade across his knees.
650305.description:
Lord Stern is a lean, silver-bearded dwarf in the faded finery of an old
noble house. He sold his city's gates to the usurper for a promise of
power, and the sleepless pallor in his eyes tells how well that bargain
has served him.

650306.name: hrodgar ironcrown usurper dwarf king
650306.long_desc: Hrodgar Ironcrown, the usurper king, stands before the great gate with a crown of black iron on his brow.
650306.description:
Hrodgar is broad as a door and nearly as hard, clad in ancient king's
plate stolen from the stronghold's vault. His beard is shot with iron
wire, and in his fist he carries a cleaver-axe that has tasted the blood
of the old royal line.

750300.name: ironcrown cleaver axe
750300.room_desc: A broad-bladed cleaver-axe of black iron lies here.
750300.description: A broad-bladed axe of black dwarven iron, its haft bound in strips of royal purple. A crown is etched on the blade, and the edge still holds a wicked shine.

750301.name: stern signet ring gold
750301.room_desc: A heavy gold signet ring lies here.
750301.description: A heavy ring of red gold set with a flat stone, bearing the crest of a stag over an anvil. The band is worn thin on the inside from long wearing.

750302.name: heartstone golem stone red
750302.room_desc: A fist-sized red stone, faintly warm, lies here.
750302.description: A fist-sized stone of deep red, scored with a ring of tiny runes. It stays faintly warm to the touch, and jewellers would pay well for it.

750303.name: tower shield iron guard
750303.room_desc: A dented iron tower shield lies here.
750303.description: A tall shield of riveted iron, scored by axe-blows. The crest of the city watch has been hammered flat on its face.

750304.name: silk cloak pale spider
750304.room_desc: A pale, glimmering cloak of spun silk lies here.
750304.description: A cloak woven from the pale silk of tunnel spiders, light as breath and surprisingly strong. It clings to the shoulders like cobweb and turns aside a glancing blow.
